objective: Package 173A registers a finite provider-neutral protected content/object-storage foundation for durable uploaded evidence, retained reference images and generated candidate ZIP bytes. This registration changes governance only; the later implementation keeps APBRA database and resource authorization authoritative and prepares a portable seam for a separately governed hosted adapter.
requirements: Jira APBRA-173 and owner architecture decision comment 10471 were refreshed on 2026-10-04. The selected preview is the full business-user journey, with Azure Container Apps Consumption, a separately triggered Job, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Blob, Key Vault, ACR and bounded Monitor/Application Insights as a reference profile. Azure is not a core product dependency, and region, SKU, spend, networking, URL, live Entra, provider use and backup targets are not selected.

Define a portable behavior-level protected content contract for exact bytes, opaque durable storage key, SHA-256 digest, expected size where applicable, verified read, immutable committed artifact, safe uncommitted cleanup and exact digest-bound evidence/reference restore. POSIX rename, fsync, file descriptors, directory paths and Azure Blob details belong to adapters, not the port.

Preserve the database as authority for company, case, request/evidence, generation attempt and artifact records. Every application read or download requires current authenticated actor, membership, exact private-resource access and the corresponding database object record before an opaque key is read. A key, guessed path, storage listing, customer email, domain, subscription or entitlement cannot grant access.

Preserve company/case/attempt binding, exact evidence and artifact identity, SHA-256 integrity, artifact expected-size check, bounded byte limits, no silent overwrite and fail-closed missing, altered, truncated or inaccessible bytes. Keep APBRA-108 candidate source-construction and validation controls intact; generated bytes changing after validation require new candidate-bound validation and governance.

Retain secure local/CI adapters: development/test-only protection where currently required, private roots and permissions, unsafe-key and symlink/traversal rejection, and exact read integrity. The alternate deterministic test adapter must exercise the same core service behavior without adapter-name business branches.

Use deployment/bootstrap dependency injection for a qualified backend; hosted operation without an injected qualified durable adapter fails closed. Storage credentials and backend choice are deployment configuration, not ordinary Tenant Settings or customer business meaning. The Azure Blob implementation and Azure SDK remain for a later separately governed APBRA-173 package.

Keep server-mediated protected reads/downloads. No public container, anonymous object URL, browser-known credential, long-lived SAS, direct key-to-byte endpoint or object-store authorization in place of APBRA authorization.

Specify a bounded database/object consistency model without pretending there is a distributed transaction: write and verify bytes before database metadata commit; only committed authoritative records expose content; cleanup of uncommitted bytes is idempotent and best effort; uncertain writes, retry, process death and cleanup failure leave at most unreachable classifiable bytes, never a successful artifact with unverifiable content. Duplicate requests may not overwrite a different committed object.

Preserve existing evidence/reference recovery only for exact original storage identity and matching digest/size. Restore cannot relabel evidence, cross a company/case boundary, replace different committed bytes or confer authority. Actual hosted backup, retention and restore qualification belongs to APBRA-173F.

Current evidence, reference and generated-artifact database rows already retain company/case (and artifact attempt), unique storage key and SHA-256 digest; generated artifacts also retain byte size. Existing keys can remain opaque adapter input. Package 173A requires no database migration and no new third-party dependency. If implementation proves either necessary, stop for a separately reviewed governance amendment rather than silently adding a path.

Registration changes exactly nine governance paths and no product/runtime file. Four historical scope tests only replace brittle tail-relative source-position assertions with exact contiguous source-ID assertions; prior source rows remain unchanged and the new rows are appended. The later implementation is limited to the exact 13 literal paths in allowed_paths, after hosted CI, genuinely separate independent exact-head review, Haseeb manual registration merge and verified post-merge main.
adrs: APBRA-175 / 04.07 deployment portability controls: Azure is a reference deployment profile; APBRA core business and domain code remains portable and customer content stays in the qualified data plane.

02.05 DATA-001/002/004/005/006/007/009 and INT-001/002 control stable identity, tenant-scoped metadata, immutable artifact/validation provenance, object-storage boundary and versioned adapters. A storage key is not an authorization token.
04.08 separates commercial entitlement, tenant policy, user permission, resource permission and validation. Neither a paid feature nor storage backend grants private content access.

The current local adapter may use POSIX hardening internally; the portable contract expresses observable correctness instead. 173D may provide an Azure Blob adapter only after separate authority, without changing the 173A domain/service contract.

Repository audit: LocalEvidenceStore in evidence.py stores both evidence and reference images; LocalArtifactStore in artifacts.py stores candidate ZIP including Delivery Guide when emitted. API constructs local stores; application.py, reference_material.py and generation.py consume them. Database records in persistence.py already retain storage keys and integrity metadata; this package does not change that schema.
acceptance_criteria: The registration PR changes exactly nine governance files, with no product code or cloud configuration. Future implementation changes only 13 unique literal paths, with no glob or unregistered runtime, test, migration, dependency or workflow path.

Evidence and reference round-trips preserve exact bytes, database metadata, digest and current case/company authorization; artifact write and authorized download preserve exact validated ZIP bytes, digest and expected size.

A foreign company/case actor, revoked membership or stale private-resource grant cannot read evidence, reference material or artifacts even when the opaque key is known; no direct public URL or SAS read path appears.

Tampered, truncated, wrong-size, missing, inaccessible or unexpectedly overwritten bytes fail closed without false successful listing/download/generation; original database evidence and safe failure provenance remain.

An object write followed by database failure leaves no exposed successful record. Cleanup may be retried idempotently; an orphan after cleanup/process failure remains unreachable and classifiable. Retry and duplicate writes cannot silently overwrite different committed content.
Exact digest-bound restore works for existing evidence/reference identity, while wrong digest, mismatched key/company/case or attempted replacement of different committed bytes is rejected.
Newly constructed application instances and two instances using the same deterministic durable adapter read previously committed bytes without process-local authority or state.

Secure local adapter retains private-root, symlink, path/traversal and permissions protections; the same core contract tests pass using secure local and deterministic alternate fake adapters without product branching.
No Azure SDK, Blob implementation, cloud resource, provider secret, migration, dependency, lockfile, public object access, Live Canvas/ARD/APBRA-165/APBRA-166 or worker queue is part of 173A.
